akhfash:18-18.t: He said ﴿قَوْماً بُوراً﴾: the plural of "البَائِر" (one who perishes), like "اليَهُود" (the Jews), whose singular is "الهَائِد". Some said: "It is a usage not based on a singular, as is said 'أَنْتَ بَشَرٌ' (you are a human) and 'أَنْتُمْ بَشَر' (you are humans)."

akhfash:19-19.t: And He said ﴿فَمَا تَسْتَطِيعُونَ صَرْفاً وَلاَ نَصْراً﴾: He omitted "from the disbelievers". It may also be about the angels. The proof that it is addressed to the disbelievers is that He said ﴿وَمَن يَظْلِم مِّنكُمْ﴾. Some said: "He means the angels."

akhfash:40-40.t: And He said ﴿ٱلَّتِيۤ أُمْطِرَتْ مَطَرَ ٱلسَّوْءِ﴾: two dialect forms; one says "مُطِرْنَا" and "أُمْطِرْنَا" (we were rained upon). And He said ﴿وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ حِجَارَةً﴾; they are two dialect forms.

akhfash:49-49.t: And He said ﴿وَأَنَاسِيَّ كَثِيراً﴾ with a doubled (yāʾ), because it is the plural of "الإِنْسِيّ" (human being).

akhfash:57-57.t: And He said ﴿إِلاَّ مَن شَآءَ﴾: an exception falling outside the first part of the speech, in the meaning of "لكنّ" (but).

akhfash:62-62.t: And He said ﴿وَٱلنَّهَارَ خِلْفَةً﴾: He means "they succeed one another".

akhfash:63-63.t: And He said ﴿وَعِبَادُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَىٰ ٱلأَرْضِ﴾: this has no khabar (predicate) except in meaning, and Allah knows best.

akhfash:74-74.t:
And He said ﴿لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَاماً﴾: "الإِمام" (leader) here is plural, as He said ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِيۤ﴾. It may also be by way of quotation, as a man says, when asked "مَنْ أميرُكُم" (who is your commander?): "هؤلاءِ أَمِيرُنا" (these are our commander). The poet said [in the kāmil metre; this is poetic witness no. 255]:
يَا عَاذِلاَتِي لا تُرِدْنَ مَلامَتي * إِنَّ العَواذِلَ لَيْسَ لِي بِأَمِير
(O my reproachers, do not seek to blame me; the reproachers are no commander over me.)

akhfash:77-77.t: And He said ﴿مَا يَعْبَأُ بِكُمْ﴾ because it is from "عَبَأْتُ بِهِ" (I cared about him), "أَنّا أَعْبَأُ بِهِ" "عَبْأً".
